neighbours.label: A present-tense statement of what something is able to do: the verb or subject just before 'can', 'easily' or 'readily' would fit ('they dissolve', 'most strains'); one-off events stay low.
fire: Salt is ionic and dissolves quickly in warm water.
These viruses travel on droplets, and most strains infect several animal species.
The roasted squash was tender and it pulled apart with a spoon.
Engineers built a tiny drone that flies through narrow gaps.
Copper is soft and bends without much force.
These weeds grow on bare soil, and many varieties spread by runners.
The folding bike is light and it fits under a desk.
Our son is two, and he climbs out of his crib.
quiet: Salt was spilled on the kitchen floor at noon.
These viruses were named in a report from the health ministry in May.
The roasted squash was served last night with a green salad.
Engineers met on Tuesday in a small room near the lab.
Copper was sold at a higher price in June.
These weeds were pulled out of the bed by a neighbour last week.
The folding bike arrived on Friday in a cardboard box.
Our son is two, and he was born in a hospital in Leeds.

predictions: 6/8 fire, 0-1 near miss. The output direction suppresses easily, readily and can on the + side, so this - pole promotes them.
notes: Probes: dissolves 0.63, reproduce 0.79, mashed with a fork 0.53, could 0.60, 'a robot that' 0.71; 'she knows her letters' 0.22, 'fits in a pocket' 0.26; events 0.01-0.06, but 'she had a cold' 0.19.
